findings.disposition_reason: lens-security round 2: protect-paths.sh:39 sets `shopt -s nocasematch` before the case at :40, so `.aegis/Answers.json` and `.AEGIS/answers.json` now hit the answers/constitution/generated arms and exit 2.
findings.message: protect-paths.sh guards `.aegis/answers.json`, the constitution and `generated/` with case-sensitive bash `case` globs, but the realpath at line 36 preserves the input's casing (posixpath.realpath only substitutes symlink targets, never on-disk canonical case). On a case-insensitive filesystem (the macOS default on this repo) an unfocused agent Writes `.aegis/Answers.json` (or `.AEGIS/answers.json`) and the write lands on the real file unrefused, defeating R-26; this is the Edit/Write path the hook exists to cover and the same class as the `..`/symlink variants the file's own comments say were fixed. The lease hook only backstops focused agents, so nothing else stops the orchestrator/doc-manager.
findings.minimal_fix: add `shopt -s nocasematch` before the case (covers answers.json, constitution, generated/).

findings.disposition_reason: lens-security round 2: flow.py:254 matches `rel.lower()` against lowercased zones; folding both sides can only merge distinct names, so it widens the refused set and never narrows it.
findings.message: `lease_violation` matches frozen zones with `matches_any`->`glob_regex`, which compiles without re.IGNORECASE, so on a case-insensitive FS an unfocused agent writing `Vendor/lib.py` into frozen `vendor/**` is not refused, though R-23 requires refusal 'focused or not'. Advisory only: `check_trace` still sees the tracked path at the gate, so the write cannot reach merge unnoticed; `nocasematch` in protect-paths does not cover this Python path.

`apply_waivers` downgrades a blocking check to `warn` for any unexpired waiver of a waivable kind with no requirement that `owner` be a person, unlike the `finding` waivers `_dismissal_problems` hardened; this repo's live `.aegis/waivers.json` shows the consequence — both entries are owned by "claude-session TASK-UNBLOCK-01 (pending human review)", a name the gate itself rejects for a review finding, and one of them mutes a `budget` failure about that session's own oversized security report. Advisory: R-25 governs only `finding` waivers and the schema deliberately permits the other kinds, so the builder may decline this in writing.
findings.minimal_fix: either require `_names_a_person(owner)` for every waiver, or have apply_waivers label an agent-owned waiver provisional in its note.

findings.message: `disposition` accepts any non-empty `--by` after strip, so `--by x` dismisses a sev-5 finding while a waiver's `owner` must be at least 2 characters — the two names carrying the same decision are held to different shapes. Observation only: per R-21 the name is a recorded claim, not an authentication, so a short or generic name like `bot` passing is the documented limit rather than a defect.
findings.minimal_fix: require len(by.strip()) >= 2 in `disposition`, matching the waiver owner's minLength.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-security round 2: `_dismissal_problems` (flow.py:1042-1077) now requires a non-agent `--by` for `false-positive` as well as waived/deferred, and check_reviews calls it for every finding at :1203.
findings.message: An agent-asserted `false-positive` permanently closes a sev>=3 first-strike finding with no person and no waiver: `disposition()` accepts any `--by` for false-positive, `check_reviews` person-gates only waived/deferred (line 1162) and reopened (1126), and `lens_record` keeps false-positive sticky on re-raise so it never becomes a second strike. Observation, not a violation: R-21/R-25 are silent on first-strike false-positive.
findings.minimal_fix: if tightening, require a person's --by for false-positive on sev>=3.
